post.summary:
Changes the password of whoever asks. Every other session of the account
ends; the one that asked goes on.

204.description: The account has the new password.

403.description: The current password is wrong.

422.description: The new password will not do.

get.summary:
Whether the account signed in here has a second step, and how many
recovery codes it has left.

post.summary:
Begins giving the account a second step: makes a secret for an
authenticator app. Nothing changes until a code from that app has been
typed back, which shows the app has it.

409.description: The account has a second step already.

post.summary:
Turns the second step on, given a code from the app that was just set up.
The answer is the account's recovery codes, which are not shown again.

409.description: No app is being set up.

422.description: The code is not the app's.

post.summary: Turns the second step of the account that asks off, given its password.

204.description: The account signs in with its password alone.

403.description: The password is wrong.

get.summary:
What was done through the panel, the newest first, a hundred lines at a
time. The one request the Activity page needs.

parameters.name: server
parameters.description: Only what was done to the server with this id.

parameters.name: user
parameters.description: Only what the account with this id did.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Only what is older than the line with this id: for the page after the first.

403.description: The account is not the owner's.

get.summary:
The Gate, how the tunnel to it is doing, and every port it forwards. The
one request the Network page needs, and the one the Gate's pill asks again.

post.summary:
Starts connecting a VPS: makes the keys of a tunnel to it and answers with
the one command to run there. The command counts for a quarter of an hour.
Core dials the VPS from now until then, and the tunnel is up within a few
seconds of the command being run; asking for the Gate again shows it.

201.description: The command is ready, and the VPS is awaited.

409.description: A Gate is connected already.

422.description: The address or the port will not do.

delete.summary:
Forgets the Gate and takes home's end of the tunnel down. Servers go back
to being reached on the home network only. The VPS keeps its Gate program
until `homewarp-gate leave` is run there.

204.description: There is no Gate now.

post.summary:
Finds out again whether servers see their players' own addresses, and puts
the Gate in the mode that works. It takes a few seconds, during which new
connections may be turned away.

409.description: No Gate is connected, or it cannot be reached.

204.description: Signed out.

get.summary: Every server, by name. The one request the Servers page needs.

post.summary:
Makes a server from a template, then installs and starts it. The answer
comes at once; the install goes on, and the server's console shows it.

409.description: The name or the port belongs to another server.

422.description: Something asked for will not do.

get.summary:
One server, with its state and the end of its console. A page that stays
open asks again to follow both.

put.summary:
Changes what a server is made of. It has to be stopped first, and what was
changed counts from its next start.

409.description: The server is running, or the name or the port belongs to another.

422.description: Something asked for will not do.

delete.summary: Removes a server that is not running, with its files.

204.description: The server and its files are gone.

409.description: The server is running.

get.summary:
A server's backups, the newest first, and how many are kept. The one
request the Backups tab needs.

403.description: The account has not been let do this.

post.summary:
Begins a backup of everything in a server's files. The answer comes at
once, with the backup as it stands; asking for the backups again shows how
it went. A server that runs meanwhile goes on running.

403.description: The account has not been let do this.

409.description: A backup of it is being made already.

422.description: The name will not do.

put.summary:
Says how many finished backups of a server are kept. It counts from the
next backup that is done: none goes because of this alone.

204.description: That many are kept from now on.

403.description: The account has not been let do this.

422.description: It is not a number from 1 to 20.

delete.summary: Deletes a backup. It cannot be brought back.

204.description: The backup is gone.

403.description: The account has not been let do this.

404.description: There is no such server, or no such backup.

409.description: The backup is still being made.

get.summary: A backup's file as it is: a tar packed with Zstandard, for the browser to save.

403.description: The account has not been let do this.

404.description: There is no such server, or no such backup.

409.description: The backup was not finished.

post.summary:
Makes a server's files what a backup says they were: everything in them
now goes, and the backup is unpacked in their place. The server has to be
stopped. The answer comes at once; the server shows as being restored
until it is done, and its console says how it went.

202.description: The backup is being put back.

403.description: The account has not been let do this.

404.description: There is no such server, or no such backup.

409.description: The server is running, or the backup was not finished.

post.summary: Types one line into the console of a server that is starting or running.

204.description: The line is on its way to the server.

409.description: The server is not running.

422.description: That is not one line.

get.summary: What is in one folder of a server's files: folders first, then by name.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: A path from the top of the server's files. Empty, or left out, is the top itself.

403.description: The path leads out of the server's files.

404.description: There is no such server, or no such folder.

422.description: That is not a folder.

get.summary:
A file's text, for the editor. A file that is not text, or is longer than
four megabytes, is refused: those are for downloading.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: A path from the top of the server's files. Empty, or left out, is the top itself.

403.description: The path leads out of the server's files.

404.description: There is no such server, or no such file.

422.description: That is not a file of text, or it is too long.

put.summary:
Writes a file: an upload, or what the editor saves. The body is the file as
it is. It takes the place of a file that is there by that name, and only
once all of it has arrived; the folders it sits in are made if they are not there.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: A path from the top of the server's files. Empty, or left out, is the top itself.

204.description: The file is there.

403.description: The path leads out of the server's files.

409.description: The disk has no room for it.

422.description: That is no path for a file, or the upload was cut off.

get.summary: A file as it is, to be saved by the browser and never shown by it.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: A path from the top of the server's files. Empty, or left out, is the top itself.

403.description: The path leads out of the server's files.

404.description: There is no such server, or no such file.

422.description: That is not a file.

post.summary: Makes a folder.

204.description: The folder is there.

403.description: The path leads out of the server's files.

409.description: Something by that name is there already.

422.description: That is no path for a folder.

post.summary:
Moves a file or a folder, which is also how it is given another name.
Never onto something that is there already.

204.description: It is where it was asked to be.

403.description: A path leads out of the server's files.

404.description: There is no such server, or nothing at `from`.

409.description: Something is at `to` already.

422.description: One of the two is no path in the server's files.

post.summary:
Packs files and folders into one gzipped tar, in the folder they are in.
The answer comes when it is done, which for a world takes a while.

403.description: A path leads out of the server's files.

404.description: There is no such server, or one of the names is not there.

409.description: The disk has no room for it.

422.description: Nothing was named, or one of the names is not one.

post.summary:
Deletes files, and folders with all that is in them. They cannot be
brought back. It stops at the first that cannot be deleted.

204.description: They are gone.

403.description: A path leads out of the server's files.

404.description: There is no such server, or one of them is not there.

422.description: One of them is no path in the server's files.

post.summary:
Unpacks a zip, a tar or a gzipped tar into the folder it is in, over what is
there by the same names. The answer comes when it is done.

403.description: The path leads out of the server's files.

404.description: There is no such server, or no such file.

409.description: The disk has no room for what is in it.

422.description: That is not an archive Homewarp can read.

get.summary:
How much of the disk a server's files take, and how much of it is left.
Every file is asked, so a page should not wait for this before it paints.

post.summary:
Starts, stops or kills a server, or installs one again whose install failed.
The answer comes once the request is on its way, not once it is carried out.

204.description: The server has been asked.

409.description: The state the server is in rules that out.

get.summary: A server's schedules, by name. The one request the Schedules tab needs.

403.description: The account has not been let do this.

post.summary: Makes a schedule.

403.description: The account has not been let do this.

409.description: The server has as many schedules as it may.

422.description: Something asked for will not do.

put.summary: Changes a schedule. When it runs next is worked out afresh.

403.description: The account has not been let do this.

404.description: There is no such server, or no such schedule.

422.description: Something asked for will not do.

204.description: The schedule is gone.

403.description: The account has not been let do this.

404.description: There is no such server, or no such schedule.

post.summary:
Sets a schedule off now, whatever its times and whether or not it is
enabled. The answer comes at once; the schedule says what the run came to.

403.description: The account has not been let do this.

404.description: There is no such server, or no such schedule.

get.summary:
The accounts that have been let into a server, by name. The owner is not
among them: it is in every server.

403.description: The account is not the owner's.

put.summary:
Lets an account into a server, or changes what it may do there. With no
permission named it may look, and no more.

204.description: The account may do what was named, and no more.

403.description: The account asking is not the owner's.

404.description: There is no such server, or no such account.

422.description: It is the owner's account.

delete.summary: Takes an account out of a server. To that account the server is then not there.

204.description: The account is out of the server.

403.description: The account asking is not the owner's.

404.description: That account was not in that server.

get.summary:
Who is signed in, and whether setup is still to do. The one request a page
needs before it can paint.

What is set. The one request the owner's part of the Settings page needs
beside the accounts.

403.description: The account is not the owner's.

put.summary:
Changes what is set. Where servers look names up counts from each
server's next start: one that is running goes on asking where it asked.

403.description: The account is not the owner's.

422.description: A resolver is not an address servers can reach.

post.summary: Creates the first account and signs it in. Works once.

200.description: The account exists and is signed in.

403.description: The setup code is wrong.

409.description: There is an account already.

422.description: The username or password will not do.

get.summary: Every template, by name. The one request the Templates page needs.

post.summary: Reads an egg and keeps it as a template.

409.description: There is a template of that name already.

422.description: This is not an egg Homewarp can read.

204.description: The template is gone.

409.description: A server is made from it.

get.summary: Every account, the owner's first. The one request the Users page needs.

403.description: The account is not the owner's.

post.summary: Makes an account. It can sign in at once, and sees no server until it is let into one.

403.description: The account is not the owner's.

409.description: There is an account by that name already.

422.description: The username or password will not do.

delete.summary: Removes an account, signs it out everywhere and takes it out of every server.

204.description: The account is gone.

403.description: The account asking is not the owner's.

409.description: It is the owner's account.

put.summary:
Gives an account another password, for whoever has forgotten theirs. The
account is signed out wherever it was signed in.

204.description: The account has the new password.

403.description: The account asking is not the owner's.

422.description: The password will not do.

delete.summary:
Turns another account's second step off: for whoever has lost both their
app and their recovery codes.

204.description: The account signs in with its password alone.

403.description: The account asking is not the owner's.

Account.description: An account, as the owner sees it among the others.

created_at.description: When it was made, in Unix seconds.

servers.description: How many servers it has been let into. The owner is in all of them, and this says nothing of it.

action.description: What was done, as a name such as `server.start` or `files.remove`.

detail.description: What it was done with: a path, a name, a command.

server.description: That server's name at the time.

server_id.description: The server it was done to, if it was done to one.

user_id.description: Whose account did it. None once that account has been removed.

username.description: That account's name at the time.

created_at.description: When it was begun, in Unix seconds.

problem.description: Why it failed, if it did.

size_bytes.description: How long the file is. Nothing until it is done.

Backups.description: A server's backups, and how many of them are kept.

kept.description: When one more is done, the oldest beyond this many go.

command.description: One line, as it would be typed into the server's console.

free_bytes.description: What is left on the disk they are on.

used_bytes.description: What the server's files take of the disk.

oneOf.description:
Where things stand. It comes first, and again for a page that has
fallen too far behind to be caught up line by line.

first.description: The number of the first of `lines`.

oneOf.description: One more line of the console.
About once a second while the server runs.

Event.description: What a page that follows a server is sent, over its socket.

ExtraPort.description: A further port of a server: voice chat, say, or the port it is queried on.

modified.description: When it was last changed, in Unix seconds.

size.description: In bytes. Nothing for what is not a file.

path.description: Where the new folder goes. The folders it sits in are made with it.

ForwardedPort.description: A port of a server, which a connected Gate forwards.

traffic_bytes.description:
What the Gate counted through it in the last day, both ways together.
Nothing where no Gate has counted.

GateView.description: The Gate, and how the tunnel to it is doing.

address.description: The VPS's public address: what players type.

command.description: While a VPS is awaited: what to run on it, as root.

expires_at.description: When that command stops counting, in Unix seconds.

handshake_age_seconds.description: How long ago the Gate last heard from home over the tunnel.

latency_ms.description: How long the way to the Gate and back takes, in milliseconds.

note.description: What the check of that found, where it needs saying.

player_addresses.description: Whether servers see their players' own addresses.

ports.description: Every port of every server: what a connected Gate forwards.

problem.description: Why the Gate could not be reached, when it could not.

reachable.description: Whether the Gate answered through the tunnel when it was last asked.

received_bytes.description: Through the tunnel since the Gate last set it up, as the Gate counts.

version.description: The version of the Gate program on the VPS.

permissions.description: What the account may do with the server beyond looking at it. None is looking only.

egg.description: The egg as a panel exports it: JSON or YAML.

code.description:
The code of the second step, for an account that has one: from its
authenticator app, or one of its recovery codes.

to.description: Where it goes, its own name included: the same folder for a new name.

password.description: What it signs in with at first. Whoever it is for can change it.

name.description: What to call it. Something is made up if nothing is given.

NewGate.description: What it takes to start connecting a VPS.

address.description: The VPS's public IPv4 address, or a name for it.

wg_port.description: The UDP port its WireGuard is to listen on. 51820 if none is given.

current.description: The password as it is now.

password.description: The one to have from now on.

folder.description: The folder the archive is made in.

names.description: What goes into it: names in that folder.

name.description: The archive's name, in the folder it was asked for in.

Permission.description: Something an account may be let do with a server, beyond looking at it.

PlayerAddresses.description: Whether servers see their players' own addresses, as the self-probe found it.

PortProtocol.description: Which protocols a port is published for at home and forwarded for by the Gate.

Power.description: What a person can ask of a server.

ProblemBody.description: The body of every error response.

code_required.description: True when what is missing is the code of the second step of a sign-in.

error.description: A sentence fit to show to the person using the panel.

RecoveryCodes.description:
The codes that sign an account in when its app is lost. Each works once,
and they are shown this one time.

paths.description: Files, and folders with all that is in them.

cron.description: When it runs, as cron writes it: minute, hour, day, month, weekday.

last_result.description: What the last run came to, in a sentence.

next_run_at.description: When it runs next, in Unix seconds. Never, while it is not enabled.

only_running.description: Whether a time at which the server is not running is passed over.

utc_offset.description: The clock those are read on: minutes east of UTC.
The clock of whoever sets it: minutes east of UTC.

Server.description: A server in full, with the end of its console.

console.description: The last lines of its console: the install first, then what the server prints.

cpu_percent.description: 100 is one core. 0 is no limit.

created_at.description: When it was made, in Unix seconds.

eula.description: Whether the game's EULA was agreed to for it.

permissions.description: What the account that asks may do with it, beyond looking at it.

port.description: Where players reach it, on the home machine and on a connected VPS.

protocol.description: Which protocols that port is open for.

template.description: The name of the template it was made from.

variables.description: The value of each of the template's variables, by the name the server sees.

ServerSettings.description: What a server is made of that can still be changed once it is made.

cpu_percent.description: 100 is one core. Nothing, or 0, is no limit.

eula.description: Whoever asks agrees to the EULA of the game, for a game that has one.

image.description: One of the template's images. Its first, if none is named.

port.description: Published on the home machine, and forwarded by a connected VPS.

ports.description: Further ports, each published and forwarded as the first is.

protocol.description: Which protocols that port is open for. Both, if none is named.

variables.description:
Values for the template's variables, by the name the server sees. One
that is not given takes the template's default.

ServerSummary.description: A server as the Servers page shows it.

port.description: Where players reach it on the home machine.

template.description: The name of the template it was made from.

ServerUser.description: An account that has been let into a server.

permissions.description: What it may do there beyond looking.

Session.description: Everything the web interface needs to decide what to show first.

setup_required.description: True until the first account has been created.

sftp_port.description: The port SFTP is reached on at this machine, where it is served.

oneOf.description: Who is signed in, if anyone.

resolvers.description:
Where servers look names up: one to three IPv4 addresses on the
internet. A change counts from each server's next start.

code.description: The code Homewarp wrote to its log when it started.

Task.description: One thing a schedule does. They are done in the order they are given in.

command.description: The line to type, for a command. Nothing for anything else.

wait_seconds.description:
How long to wait before it, in seconds: after the task before it, or
after the time came for the first.

Template.description: A template in full: everything Homewarp will do on its word.

config_files.description: The files patched in a server's directory before every start.

created_at.description: When it was imported, in Unix seconds.

done.description: A server has started once its console prints any of these.

images.description: The first is the one a new server runs in unless another is picked.

oneOf.description: What runs once, before a server's first start. Not every template has it.

startup.description: The command that starts a server, with `{{NAME}}` where a variable goes.

TemplateStop.description: How a server is asked to shut down.

value.description: The command typed into the console, or the name of the signal sent.

TemplateSummary.description: A template as the gallery shows it.

image.description: The image a new server runs in unless another is picked.

env.description: The environment variable the server sees.

rules.description: Laravel-style validation rules, one per entry.

TwoSteps.description: Whether the account that asks has a second step to its sign-in.

recovery_codes.description: How many of its recovery codes have not been used.

TwoStepsSetup.description: What an authenticator app is given to make the codes of an account.

secret.description: The secret, to type into the app.

uri.description: The same as a link, which an app on this device opens.

path.description: A zip, a tar or a gzipped tar. It is unpacked into the folder it is in.

skipped.description:
How many entries were left out: those that would have gone outside the
server's files, and what is neither a file, a folder nor a link.

Usage.description: How much of the machine a running server is using.

cpu_percent.description: Of one core: 150 is a core and a half.

memory_limit_bytes.description: The most it may use before it is stopped.

owner.description:
The account made at setup. It may do everything; any other account
only what it has been let do, with the servers it has been let into.
